Receive Task

General Concept: A Receive Task in BPMN is used to wait for a message from an external participant or system before continuing the process. It is typically used for inbound communication, such as receiving events, data, or signals.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Receive Task waits for a message using a configured message handler. Input mappings can be defined using FEEL expressions to process the received data. Receive Tasks support correlation, error handling, and timeouts. Variable scoping ensures only mapped variables are updated. The engine can interact with messaging systems, APIs, or custom adapters for inbound communication.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Receive Task in TaktX allows you to:

  • Wait for incoming messages or signals to continue the process.
  • Define input mappings using FEEL expressions for correlation and data extraction.
  • Configure error handling and process interruption if a message is not received.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for event-driven process steps and external triggers.

 

Example: Payment Confirmation with Receive Task

 

This example shows a process where an order is placed, a Receive Task waits for payment confirmation, and the process continues to shipment. The Receive Task demonstrates waiting for an external event before proceeding.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions to validate and process received data.
  • Configure correlation for reliable message matching.
  • Handle errors and timeouts to avoid process interruptions.
  • Document message formats and endpoints.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmatched messages will not trigger the task.
  • Unmapped variables will not be updated.
  • Message loss or delays can block process progress.
